t: G37 Gaming Engine: Frame Budget Desk — Simple
name: G37 Gaming Engine: Frame Budget Desk — Simple
title: G37 Gaming Engine: Frame Budget Desk — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] 60 fps gives 16.67 ms per frame, split between update and render. The desk allocates the budget per system — physics, AI, render — and verifies the worst-case sum fits. A frame that overruns is a dropped frame, and the budget is what prevents it.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Frame period at 60 fps = 16.667 ms. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.

real_world_basis: Frame budgeting is the real discipline of game engineering.
signature_version: Signature version: the PIC_Game frame desk — the chapter's Player Immersion Constant as the frame-time target, with the perpetual framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: measure worst-case, not average — averages drop frames.
math_note: Frame period at 60 fps: 16.667 ms [verified]; Frame period at 120 fps: 8.333 ms [verified]
safety: No hazard; the failure mode is a beautiful game at 20 fps.
how_it_works: List the per-system worst-case costs, sum them, and require the total under the frame period with margin. The demo budgets a 60 fps action game.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub
